author: Mataeo Smith
title: Hazmat squad raids California home, finds mysterious items that spark FBI investigation - NewsBreak
text:
By Mataeo Smith ,
1 hours ago Police in Irvine got a call from a worried homeowner who reported strange activity, prompting the dispatch of a hazmat squad.
On Monday, police were called to a residence on Cartwheel after receiving a report of suspicious activity there. Police called the Orange County Fire Authority for assistance from its hazmat team after examining the area and concluding that items at the residence needed additional assessment. The FBI arrived on the scene later that night and assumed control of the investigation.
“The FBI’s Evidence Response Team and Hazardous Evidence Response Team responded to a residence in Irvine, California at the request of the Orange County Fire Authority,” the federal agency said in a statement. “The FBI continues to work this matter jointly with the Irvine Police Department, the Orange County Fire Authority and the Orange County Sheriff’s Department. There is no known threat to public safety. As this is an ongoing investigation, we are not able to provide additional information at this time.”

What law enforcement is looking into is unclear.
This comes after the federal response to a bio lab discovered in a Fresno County suburb earlier this month was questioned by California officials after a similar setup was discovered at a Las Vegas residence over the weekend.
In late 2023, the California lab was discovered in a Reedley residence. According to police, the illicit laboratory had over 1,000 mice that were allegedly used as test subjects in addition to "pathogen-labeled containers" with labels that included dengue fever, HIV, and malaria.
Chinese national Jia Bei Zhu was detained in October 2023 and charged in November. He is still incarcerated after being accused of spreading contaminated and mislabeled medical supplies, including coronavirus testing. In April, he is scheduled to appear in court.
A similar setup was discovered inside a Las Vegas residence that authorities raided. Police discovered "multiple refrigerators, a freezer, and other laboratory-type equipment, along with numerous bottles and jugs containing unknown liquid substances" inside a closed garage, according to Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department sheriff Kevin McMahill.
"These items, importantly, were consistent in appearance to the items found and described in the Reedley, California lab investigation," McMahill said.

Agents discovered a centrifuge, biosafety equipment, and "unknown liquids in gallon-sized containers and refrigerated vials with unknown liquids," according to FBI Special Agent in Charge for Las Vegas Christoper Delzotto." According to Delzotto, more than 1,000 samples were taken from the scene and sent to the National Bioforensic Analysis Center in Maryland.
According to McMahill, before to the raid, the police department "received limited information that laboratory equipment and potentially hazardous materials" were being kept in the Vegas residence.
